title: How To Start a T-Shirt Business: 2026 Guide
summary: Looking to sell t-shirts? Read expert tips on finding customers, designing graphics, and selling shirts online.
body_markdown:
An online t-shirt business can use print on demand, buy finished inventory in batches, or print garments in-house.


The custom t-shirt printing market was valued at[$5.82 billion in 2025](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/t-shirt-printing-market-114878) and is expected to grow by[12.81% annually through 2034](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/t-shirt-printing-market-114878) . Globally, t-shirts generate more than[$46 billion](https://www.statista.com/outlook/cmo/apparel/men-s-apparel/t-shirts/worldwide) in annual revenue, driven by rising demand for casual, comfortable clothing.


With online tools to help you[print and sell t-shirts](https://www.shopify.com/sell/tshirts) , it's never been easier to start a t-shirt business. This guide explains seven steps to starting an online shirt business that generates monthly income.


## How to start a t-shirt business: 7 steps


1. Choose a niche
2. Source materials and printing partners
3. Create t-shirt designs
4. Mock up your t-shirts
5. Validate your t-shirt designs
6. Register your business and write a plan
7. Set up your online store


### 1. Choose a niche


Successful online t-shirt businesses find ways to stand out from the crowd. One of the best strategies for differentiating your products from those of your competitors is by catering to a specific audience or interest group.


Choosing a t-shirt[niche](https://www.shopify.com/blog/niche-markets) can help your online shirt business attract these motivated customers.


Generally, niches like "t-shirts with funny slogans" are too broad for a new business to successfully compete. Targeting the market for "funny t-shirts" or "t-shirts for women" may pit your business against large, established rivals.


Instead, look for sub-niches and use[keyword research tools](https://www.shopify.com/blog/keyword-research-tools) to find phrases that your target audience is searching for.


For example, sub-niches in the funny t-shirts category might be "t-shirts with slogans about doctors" or "funny t-shirts for dog owners."


Getting granular with a sub-niche could be a helpful strategy for your t-shirt business. *ThinkPup*


If you're struggling to find your niche, start with a general interest topic. Then, using a[mind map](https://www.shopify.com/partners/blog/mind-map) or[brainstorming technique](https://www.shopify.com/blog/brainstorming-techniques) , think about how you can break your general topic into subtopics that have a consumer market.


For example, you might divide dogs into specific breeds, dog owner lifestyles (hiking with dogs, dog moms), or even different types of dog-related humor.


Once you have a niche in mind, estimate its market value. Here are some ways to gauge consumer interest:


- Check Google Trends to see whether interest is growing, declining, or seasonal.
- Use Google Keyword Planner or another keyword research tool to compare search volume and competition.
- Visit relevant subreddits, Facebook Groups, Discord communities, and other forums. Look at posting frequency and the responses products receive.
- Review bestselling shirts and customer reviews on marketplaces. Reviews can reveal popular themes, fit complaints, and requests competitors have not addressed.
- Use audience estimates inside advertising platforms to gauge the potential reach of specific interests.
- Interview people in the target audience or run a short survey before committing to inventory.


Remember, the more specific your niche, the easier it will be to target your marketing and connect with passionate customers.


### 2. Source materials and printing partners


The next step in starting an online t-shirt business is to source your inventory. You'll need to partner with suppliers or manufacturers that can provide the type of clothing your customers won't be able to resist.


If you plan on selling shirts made by brands and designers, you'll want to work with a[wholesale clothing supplier](https://www.shopify.com/blog/wholesale-clothing-vendors) . You can also[source products from Shopify brands](https://www.shopify.com/source-products) using Shopify Collective, Shopify's built-in supplier network that lets you browse and sell products from verified Shopify merchants without buying inventory upfront.


If you envisage selling tees with original, unique designs and graphics, you'll need a[custom tee manufacturer](https://www.shopify.com/blog/print-on-demand-shirts) .


#### Choose a t-shirt business model


Your business model determines how much inventory you buy and who prints and ships each order. Consider the following:


- **Print-on-demand.** Products are made after the purchase, but tend to have less production control and higher per-unit costs.
- **Small-batch production.** You purchase a limited quantity of stock. It offers lower unit costs but carries the risk of unsold stock.
- **Bulk production.** You buy stock in volume at a lower unit cost.
- **Curated resales.** You sell finished shirts made by other brands.


#### Printing techniques


Not all t-shirt production methods are the same. Different printing techniques produce different results. With shirt quality associated with your brand's reputation, take time to choose the right type of printing.


There are four popular methods for printing t-shirts. Deciding which one to use will depend on your[product pricing strategy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/pricing-strategies) , order volumes, and design complexity.


**Comparison of t-shirt printing methods**


Printing method Best for Cost structure Quality Durability Design complexity Minimum order


Screen printing Large orders (50+ units) Low per-unit cost for bulk High Excellent, long-lasting Limited (4–5 colors max) High minimums


Heat transfer Small batches Moderate upfront investment Medium Less than screen/DTG Full-color possible No minimums


Direct to garment (DTG) Small orders, detailed designs No setup cost, consistent per-unit pricing High Excellent on natural fibers Excellent for complex designs No minimums


Direct to film (DTF) Mixed fabrics, stretchy materials Moderate per-unit cost High Excellent on all fabrics Excellent for complex designs Low minimums


Dye sublimation Polyester performance apparel, all-over prints Moderate equipment or per-unit cost High Excellent on polyester Excellent for detailed, full-color designs Supplier dependent


##### Screen printing


An industrial screen printing machine. *Printful*


Screen printing is a technique that has stood the test of time for business owners who design and sell t-shirts online and in stores.


As one of the most popular printing methods, screen printing produces durable, long-lasting results. It also lets you print on products like canvas items, mugs, hats, and other[things to make and sell](https://www.shopify.com/blog/things-to-make-and-sell) if you want to expand your product line.


However, a labor-intensive setup means screen printing is most cost-effective for bulk printing. Screen printing also poses challenges for complex designs or those with more than four colors, as each additional color increases costs and production time.


**Best for:** Businesses ordering more than 50 shirts with simple designs and limited colors.


##### Heat transfer


You can use a heat transfer machine to print quickly. *Transfer Express*


Heat transfer is a category that covers several processes, including heat-transfer vinyl, printed transfer paper, and plastisol transfers. The process uses heat and pressure to attach a design to the garment.


A business can order finished transfers from a supplier and apply them with a heat press as orders arrive. This arrangement can work for names, numbers, small product runs, and designs that change frequently.


Costs and durability depend on the transfer material, fabric, pressing temperature, and application quality. Test the finished shirt after washing before selecting a process.


**Best for:** Entrepreneurs who want to produce small batches on demand and don't mind hands-on production.


##### Direct to garment (DTG)


Direct-to-garment printing machines are common. *Anajet*


[Direct-to-garment printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-dtg-printing) applies water-based ink directly to a shirt using a specialized printer. It can reproduce detailed, multicolor artwork with minimal preparation compared with screen printing.


DTG generally performs best on cotton and cotton-rich garments. Dark shirts often need pretreatment and white underbase ink. Polyester and some blended fabrics can produce less predictable results.


DTG equipment, maintenance, pretreatment, and curing add costs for businesses printing in-house. Print-on-demand providers typically charge a fixed unit price, though supplier discounts may apply at higher volumes.


**Best for:** Print-on-demand businesses and stores selling custom designs in small quantities on cotton garments.


##### Direct to film (DTF)


[Direct-to-film (DTF) printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/direct-to-film-printing) is a newer technology that applies custom designs to apparel via image transfer. The process involves printing a design onto a special transfer film with water-based inks, coating it with adhesive powder, and heat-pressing it onto the garment.


DTF has become increasingly popular because it works with a wide range of fabrics—including synthetics like polyester, nylon, and fleece—where DTG struggles. This makes DTF ideal for athletic wear, performance fabrics, and mixed-material garments. Learn more about[DTG versus DTF printing](https://www.shopify.com/blog/dtg-vs-dtf) to determine which method is right for your business.


DTF typically requires lower minimum orders than screen printing but has a slightly higher per-unit cost than bulk screen printing. It's a good middle-ground option for businesses needing flexibility across fabric types without committing to large inventory.


**Best for:** Businesses selling on multiple fabric types, especially athletic wear and synthetic materials, with moderate order volumes.


##### Dye sublimation


[Dye sublimation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sublimation-printing) uses heat to fuse dye with polyester fibers. The design becomes part of the material, which prevents the surface cracking associated with some transfer methods.


Sublimation can produce detailed graphics and all-over prints, but it works best on white or light-colored polyester garments. It cannot reproduce white ink on a dark shirt.


Best for: Polyester performance shirts, sportswear, and all-over designs.


#### Price vs. quality


Choosing a budget supplier and sacrificing quality for higher profits can be tempting for t-shirt sellers. But consider how product quality impacts a customer's decision to make a second purchase or[recommend your shirts](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-word-of-mouth-marketing) to other people.


Higher quality t-shirts might cost more to produce but can also command higher prices. Choosing the right quality of t-shirt means considering factors including fit, sizing, material, softness, and weight. Once you narrow down your choices, order some samples to make an informed final decision.


According to Ryan Bartlett, founder of[True Classic](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTFvv1heE2U) , investing $800 to $1,000 in quality samples and tech packs was crucial. The investment helped his brand develop a product that addressed a real gap in the men's apparel market. True Classic bootstrapped with just $3,000 in startup capital and grew into a multimillion-dollar business by prioritizing product quality from day one.


Remember to base your product quality decisions on expected[profit margin](https://www.shopify.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator) , not just the production costs.


### 3. Create t-shirt designs


Not every t-shirt business needs to sell original tees—but if you do plan to design your own line of shirts, now is the time to get creative.


Your designs don't need to be complex—in fact, many of the bestselling graphic tees are simple. However, they do need to be unique.


#### Research designs


Already inspired to produce the next big t-shirt trend? That's great! If you're struggling to come up with t-shirt design ideas, however, it can help to look at what's currently selling well. Try browsing graphic t-shirt marketplaces such as:


- [TeePublic](https://www.teepublic.com/t-shirts)
- [Threadless](https://www.threadless.com/search?sort=popular&style=t-shirt&type=regular-unisex&departments=womens)
- [SnorgTees](http://www.snorgtees.com/t-shirts/best-sellers)


Another research tip is to use[Google Trends](https://trends.google.com/trends/) to see which topics people are currently interested in. Use trending subjects as inspiration for your t-shirt designs.


Graphic t-shirts currently account for[57% of t-shirt market revenue](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/custom-t-shirt-printing-market) . This growth signals strong consumer demand for unique, personalized designs.


#### Hire a designer


Once you have a general idea for t-shirt designs, start sketching some drafts. If you can hand-draw illustrations or know how to use[graphic design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-graphic-design) software, you likely can produce great designs yourself. However, it might make more sense to enlist some help.


There are several online sources for finding suitable graphic designers, including design communities, freelance networks, and t-shirt design marketplaces.


##### Design communities


[Dribbble](https://dribbble.com/) is a design community that's home to lots of talent. Search for styles you like, then message the designer to see if they're available for your project.


Searching for designs can spark inspiration and connect you with illustrators. *Dribble*


[Behance](https://www.behance.net/) hosts portfolios from creators around the world who specialize in illustrations and graphic design.


If you find an artist you're interested in working with, you can reach out to them. *Behance*


##### Freelance networks


General freelance networks like[Upwork](https://www.upwork.com/) also contain listings of artists and illustrators. Find a qualified t-shirt designer, then check their past job successes and portfolio to see if they're a match for your project. If you like someone, you can reach out through the platform and hire them on the spot.


##### T-shirt design marketplaces


Instead of hiring a designer, you can purchase pre-made designs for your t-shirt business. This route saves on upfront costs, but means other stores are likely selling your designs, so it may be harder for your products to stand out. Check out the following t-shirt graphic marketplaces:


- [Tshirt Factory](https://tshirt-factory.com/) has a variety of vector images, from old school to punk designs.
- [Creative Market](https://creativemarket.com/) has more than three million graphics and templates.
- [GraphicRiver](http://www.graphicriver.net/) offers royalty-free Photoshop vectors and icon packs.


Keep in mind, you may need to purchase a commercial license for your images before you can use them on your t-shirts.


Follow the printer’s file specifications before submitting a design. Many printers request a transparent PNG at 300 pixels per inch, but accepted dimensions, resolution, color profile, file type, and print area vary. Vector files may be preferable for screen printing because they can be resized without losing detail.


**Need a logo for your t-shirts?** Shopify has a[free custom logo maker](https://www.shopify.com/tools/logo-maker) .


#### Check design and brand rights


Confirm that you own or have licensed every illustration, photograph, font, logo, and other element in a design. Purchasing an image does not automatically grant permission to print it on products. Read the license for commercial use, product sales, modification, exclusivity, and sales-volume limits.


A contract with a freelance designer should also specify who owns the finished work and how the business may use it. Copyright generally protects original works of authorship, whereas trademarks identify the source of goods or services. Shopify’s[guide to trademarks versus copyright](https://www.shopify.com/blog/trademark-vs-copyright) explains the difference.


Before selecting a business name or logo, search for similar marks in the countries where you plan to operate. U.S. businesses can begin with the[USPTO trademark search system](https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/search) .


Avoid using protected characters, brand logos, photographs, song lyrics, or slogans unless you have permission. Consult an intellectual property professional when ownership or licensing is unclear.


### 4. Mock up your t-shirts


Once you have final designs, the next step for your t-shirt business is to create mockup images. Mockups help you and your customers see what the final design will look like when it's printed on a shirt.


Instead of printing and photographing a sample shirt, you can give your customers a digital mockup preview—useful for stores offering hundreds of shirt designs.


You can create mockups using web software or with an image editor like Adobe Photoshop.


[T-shirt mockup templates](https://www.shopify.com/blog/19495812-22-awesome-t-shirt-templates-and-mockups-for-your-clothing-line) for Photoshop come with multiple layers that let you change the color of the shirt and apply your own design that will blend with the shirt's creases, folds, and contours.


There are also web-based mockup software that will let you create similar images without having to download Photoshop:


- [Printful mockup generator](https://www.printful.com/mockup-generator)
- [Placeit mockup generator](https://placeit.net/garment-only-mockups)
- [Printify t-shirt mockup generator](https://printify.com/mockup-generator/)


If you don't like the idea of creating digital mockups, you can always order samples of your shirts and take[product photos](https://www.shopify.com/blog/12206313-the-ultimate-diy-guide-to-beautiful-product-photography) yourself.


### 5. Validate your t-shirt designs


Before you invest in your new business idea, test the popularity of your designs. There are many ways to validate design popularity before you sell your t-shirts online.


Common methods for validating your design ideas include:


#### Collect signups


Create a landing page that previews several designs and asks interested shoppers to join a launch list.[Shopify Forms](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/forms-app) can collect contact information, tag subscribers according to their interests, and connect responses to customer segments and marketing automations.


Signups do not guarantee purchases, but they provide a stronger demand signal than likes alone. Track which design, message, or audience produces the most qualified registrations.


#### Reach out to personal social networks


Post a preview of your designs to your social media accounts and on feeds that your potential customers visit. Be careful when asking the thoughts of friends and family, however. Their opinions can come with a favorable bias.


Allegra Shaw, founder of[Uncle Studios](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qujqSDpfQo) , successfully leveraged her existing YouTube community to validate and launch her first product—a white t-shirt that became her bestselling item. With an audience that already trusted her, she launched without paid advertising and built a seven-figure clothing brand from just $5,000 in savings.


#### Ask Reddit


Despite the community's general aversion to marketing, Reddit is still one of the best places to get[honest feedback on your designs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sugoi-shirts-testing-process) . Through this process, you may earn yourself some future customers and gain some free marketing along the way.


#### Use crowdfunding


[Crowdfunding sites](https://www.shopify.com/blog/crowdfunding-sites) have made it easier to test, validate, and collect money upfront for new business ideas. Launching a crowdfunding campaign can be time-consuming and requires preparation. However, if you have a particularly novel t-shirt business idea, crowdfunding might be for you.


Here's why you should test your t-shirt designs before you invest:


### 6. Register your business and write a plan


Typically, you don't need a[business license](https://www.shopify.com/blog/business-license) to sell t-shirts online. But, you may need a resale license to buy clothing from a distributor without sales tax.


Check with your local revenue or finance department to learn about the types of licenses or registration requirements that you may be required to get.


#### Business registration


[Registering your business](https://www.shopify.com/blog/register-business) is a way of formally recognizing your t-shirt store as a legal entity. This can protect your personal assets and provide tax benefits, as well as enhance credibility with business partners, like your supplier.


The[type of business structure](https://www.shopify.com/blog/types-businesses) you choose affects how your business will be taxed, and how much of your personal assets are put at risk. Common structures include:


**Comparison of business structures**


Business structure Liability protection Tax treatment Setup complexity Best for


Sole proprietorship None (personal liability) Personal income tax on profits Very simple Testing a business idea with minimal risk


Limited liability company (LLC) Yes (protects personal assets) Pass-through taxation (or can elect corporate) Moderate Most small t-shirt businesses seeking liability protection


C corporation (C corp) Yes (protects personal assets) Double taxation (corporate + dividends) Complex Larger businesses seeking investment


- **Sole proprietorship:** A[sole proprietorship](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sole-proprietor) is the simplest form of business entity, with one owner who pays personal income tax on profits earned from the business.
- **Limited liability company (LLC):** The[LLC](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-an-llc) structure provides a small business with the protection of a[corporation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-a-corporation) , shielding owners from debts and liabilities accrued by the company.
- **C corporation (C corp):** A C corp structure protects personal assets but is subject to double taxation.


#### Business plans


While not essential, drafting an official[business plan](https://www.shopify.com/blog/business-plan) can help solidify the goals of your t-shirt business. Business plans serve as road maps, helping you outline your aims, target market, budget, and long-term strategies.


A well-thought-out business plan can also be invaluable if you ever seek funding or partnerships. A comprehensive[business plan template](https://www.shopify.com/blog/business-plan-template) can guide you through the process of documenting your vision, financial projections, and marketing strategy.


#### Pricing your t-shirts


One of the most critical elements of your business plan is determining[how to price your products](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-price-your-product) . Your pricing strategy directly impacts profitability and competitiveness. Here are three common pricing approaches for t-shirt businesses:


**Pricing formula comparison**


Pricing method Formula Example Best for


Cost-plus pricing Total costs + desired profit % $10 cost + 50% markup = $15 Straightforward pricing, ensuring consistent margins


Keystone pricing Wholesale cost × 2 $8 wholesale × 2 = $16 retail Retail businesses with standard markup expectations


Value-based pricing Price based on customer perceived value Premium brand charges $35+ based on quality/brand Unique designs, strong brand positioning, niche audiences


##### Cost-plus pricing


[Cost-plus pricing](https://www.shopify.com/retail/cost-plus-pricing) involves calculating your total costs (materials, labor, overhead, shipping) and adding your desired profit margin.


**Example:** If your t-shirt costs $10 to produce (including blank shirt, printing, packaging, and shipping), and you want a 50% profit margin:


- Cost: $10
- Markup: $10 × 0.5 = $5
- **Selling price: $15**


Typical t-shirt profit margins range from 30% to 60%, depending on your niche, quality, and production method.


##### Keystone pricing


Keystone pricing is a retail pricing strategy where you simply double the wholesale cost of a product. This rule-of-thumb approach is popular because it's easy to implement and typically delivers healthy gross margins.


**Example:** If you buy or produce a t-shirt for $8:


- Wholesale cost: $8
- Keystone markup: $8 × 2 = $16
- ****Selling price: $16****


This method works well for businesses that need consistent, predictable margins across multiple products.


##### Value-based pricing


With value-based pricing, customer perception and willingness to pay—rather than production costs—determine your price. This strategy works best for businesses with unique designs, strong brand positioning, or products solving specific problems for their target audience.


**Example:** A premium streetwear brand with exclusive designs might charge $50 per shirt, even if production costs are only $12. That's because customers value the brand, design uniqueness, and community association.


Value-based pricing requires deep understanding of your[target market](https://www.shopify.com/blog/target-market) and strong brand differentiation, but can deliver the highest profit margins.


Use Shopify's[profit margin calculator](https://www.shopify.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator) to experiment with different pricing scenarios and understand how costs impact your bottom line.


### 7. Set up your online store


With your t-shirt designs commissioned, mock-ups created, and feedback acquired, it's time to[build your online store](https://www.shopify.com/website/builder) .


Setting up an online store might sound daunting, but it's really just a series of simple steps that anyone can follow:


#### Domain names


Think of a[domain name](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-a-domain) like your home address on the internet—it's how your customers find you.


Choose a name that's short, catchy, and easy to remember. Ideally, your domain should reflect your brand and the fact that your store specializes in t-shirts. Once you've picked a name,[register it](https://www.shopify.com/domains) to make it officially yours.


#### Building your site


Creating a website is your chance to make a great first impression, so it's important to get it right. Use a drag-and-drop[store builder](https://www.shopify.com/start) to build a professional-looking site, complete with product pages, collections, and information about your brand. Choose a[store theme](https://themes.shopify.com/themes) aligned with your shirts' style.


Each product page needs:


- Front, back, and detail photographs
- Available colors and sizes
- Garment measurements and a size chart
- Fabric composition and weight
- Fit information
- Print method and placement
- Care instructions
- Production and shipping estimates
- Return and exchange policies


Shopify product variants can organize size and color combinations and track inventory for each version. Apparel category metafields can store fabric, size, neckline, sleeve length, and color information. Compatible themes can display colors as swatches.


Product metafields can also display[size charts and care instructions](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/custom-data/metafields/pop-up-tutorial) . Use[Shopify Search & Discovery](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/storefront-search/search-and-discovery-filters) to add collection filters for size, color, availability, price, fabric, and other product attributes.


Focus on making your site easy to navigate, with clear categories and a simple[checkout process](https://www.shopify.com/checkout) .


Build an online store with AI


Create a website in minutes with the AI store builder. Describe your brand or products to generate a free custom theme that fits your idea.


[Try it now](https://www.shopify.com/tools/ai-store-builder)


#### Other sales channels


While your website will become the main hub for your brand and product collection, don't overlook other platforms where you can reach customers.


Marketplaces like[Etsy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/etsy-and-shopify) ,[Amazon](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sell-on-amazon) , and[eBay](https://www.shopify.com/blog/sell-on-ebay) are great for expanding your presence. When you run a Shopify store, you can quickly list your products on marketplaces and manage them from your store dashboard, using the[Marketplace Connect app](https://apps.shopify.com/search?q=etsy) .


Having a multichannel presence helps you reach customers wherever they prefer to shop.


#### Connecting a print-on-demand app


If you're using a[print-on-demand service](https://www.shopify.com/print-on-demand) to produce your tees, it's easy to integrate your products with a Shopify store. Simply choose and[download a print-on-demand app](https://apps.shopify.com/categories/finding-products-product-sourcing-print-on-demand-pod) .


Once integrated, customers can then visit your store to browse your tees. When they make a purchase, your print-on-demand partner will produce and ship the items.


Try these t-shirt printing apps that integrate directly with Shopify stores:


- [Printful](https://apps.shopify.com/printful) . Industry leader with extensive product catalog and warehousing options.
- [Gelato](https://apps.shopify.com/gelato-print-on-demand) . Global print network with local production in 32 countries for fast shipping.
- [Printify](https://apps.shopify.com/printify) . Access to more than 90 print providers with competitive pricing.
- [Teelaunch](https://apps.shopify.com/teelaunch-1) . Premium quality printing with no monthly fees.
- [Apliiq](https://apps.shopify.com/apliiq) . Unique branding options including custom labels and packaging.


Print on demand is particularly attractive for new entrepreneurs because it requires minimal upfront investment. You only pay for products after customers place orders, eliminating inventory risk entirely.


## How to market your t-shirt business?


You can market your t-shirt business through social media marketing, influencer partnerships, and email marketing once your store is live. Here are proven marketing strategies for t-shirt businesses:


### Social media marketing


Platforms like Instagram, TikTok, and Pinterest are visual-first channels perfect for showcasing t-shirt designs. Post lifestyle photos, behind-the-scenes content, and customer testimonials to build engagement. Learn more about creating an effective[marketing plan](https://www.shopify.com/blog/marketing-plan) for your business.


### Influencer partnerships


Collaborate with micro-influencers (1,000 to 100,000 followers) in your niche. These creators often have highly engaged audiences and charge reasonable rates or may accept free products in exchange for authentic promotion.


### Content marketing


Create blog posts, videos, or social content around topics your target audience cares about. For example, a dog-themed t-shirt brand might create content about dog training, dog care tips, or funny dog stories. Explore more[marketing strategies](https://www.shopify.com/blog/topics/marketing) to grow your business.


### Email marketing


Build an email list from day one. Offer a discount code for first-time subscribers, then send regular updates featuring new designs, customer stories, and exclusive offers.


[Shopify Messaging](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/promoting-marketing/create-marketing/shopify-messaging) can send email, SMS, and WhatsApp campaigns from Shopify. Availability and pricing vary by channel and country. T-shirt sellers can use automations for welcome offers, abandoned checkouts, product launches, restocks, and customer win-back campaigns.


### Paid advertising


Once you validate product-market fit, invest in paid ads on Facebook, Instagram, or Google. Start with small budgets ($5 to $10 per day) and test different audiences and creative variations.[True Classic's founders](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTFvv1heE2U) allocated $2,000 of their initial $3,000 budget to Facebook ads and carefully tracked return on ad spend to stay profitable.


### Partnership marketing


Like Michelle K. Hanabusa's clothing brand,[Uprisers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yYj4Y3u9T8M) , consider partnerships with complementary businesses or organizations that align with your brand values. This can help you reach new audiences.


## How did an anime-inspired t-shirt store succeed?


Anime-inspired t-shirt store Imouri grew into a six-figure print-on-demand business by testing designs with Reddit and paid ads. For example, Ryan McCarthy, founder of[Imouri](https://imouri.com/) (formerly Sugoi), has used Shopify to run his anime-inspired t-shirt printing business since 2016.


Imouri uses Shopify to power its online store. *Imouri*


Ryan decided to create his t-shirt business when he couldn't find anime-themed clothing that fit his personal style. He quietly launched what he thought would be a small clothing business, which has since turned into a six-figure print-on-demand apparel company selling streetwear inspired by Japanese pop culture and anime.


His secret to successfully starting a clothing line? Identifying winning designs early on by using Reddit and paid ads to test products.

## T-shirt business FAQ


### How much does it cost to start a t-shirt business?


Starting a t-shirt business from home requires little investment. Print-on-demand services offer product manufacturing and shipping, and only charge vendors for products when they're sold. That means fewer overhead costs and little risk of overstocking. Successful entrepreneurs like Ryan Bartlett of[True Classic started with just $3,000 total investment](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gTFvv1heE2U) —$800 to $1,000 for samples and $2,000 for initial marketing. Allegra Shaw built[Uncle Studios into a seven-figure brand starting with just $5,000](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1qujqSDpfQo) . You can also[start a business without money](https://www.shopify.com/blog/start-business-without-money) using print on demand.


### How much can you make selling t-shirts?


The amount you make selling t-shirts depends on factors including your chosen niche, production methods, pricing, and marketing strategy. Typical t-shirt profit margins range from 30% to 60%. A small business selling 100 shirts per month at $25 each with a 40% profit margin would generate $10,000 in monthly revenue and $4,000 in profit. Successful t-shirt businesses can scale to six or seven figures annually with the right product-market fit and marketing.


### Is a t-shirt business profitable?


A t-shirt business can be profitable, and it sits in a market where[global apparel sales reached $1.84 trillion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/apparel-market-report) in 2025. Creating an online t-shirt business can be profitable thanks to[low startup costs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/low-cost-business-ideas-with-high-profit) compared to other business opportunities. The custom t-shirt printing market alone is[valued at $5.82 billion and growing at 12.81% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/t-shirt-printing-market-114878) . Profitability depends on finding a specific niche, maintaining healthy profit margins (30% to 60%), and implementing effective marketing strategies.


### How do I market my t-shirt business online?


Try social media marketing on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, and Facebook. Social marketing channels include running ads, collaborating with micro-influencers (those with 1,000 to 100,000 followers), and posting engaging content (images, videos, customer testimonials). Build an email list from day one to nurture relationships with customers. Consider partnerships with complementary brands or organizations that share your target audience. Start with organic content to validate your designs, then invest in paid advertising once you have proven winners. Learn more about[how to build a brand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-build-a-brand) that resonates with your audience.


### What are the best t-shirt printing methods for small businesses?


Small businesses can start with print-on-demand, then move to DTG or DTF printing for small runs and screen printing for large orders. Direct-to-garment (DTG) printing offers high quality and is good for small batches on cotton and natural fiber garments. Direct-to-film (DTF) printing works across a wider range of fabrics including synthetics and is ideal for athletic wear. Screen printing is cost-effective for large orders (more than 50 units) but requires higher minimums. Choose based on your business model:[print on demand](https://www.shopify.com/blog/print-on-demand-companies) for testing, DTG or DTF for small-to-medium runs, and screen printing when you're ready to scale with proven designs.


### What should I do before selling t-shirts?


1. Conduct market research on a niche and find a passionate community.
2. Come up with a t-shirt company name.
3. Make a business logo and set up an online shop.
4. Create your own t-shirt designs or source pre-made graphics.
5. Order samples to validate quality.
6. Set up your social media accounts.
7. Validate designs with your target audience through social media, Reddit, or crowdfunding.
8. Plan your pricing strategy using cost-plus, keystone, or value-based pricing models.
9. Connect with print-on-demand partners or manufacturers.
10. Build a[marketing plan](https://www.shopify.com/blog/marketing-plan) focused on your niche audience.


### How can I start my own t-shirt business with few upfront costs?


If you want to[start a t-shirt business without a significant initial investment](https://www.shopify.com/blog/10580693-how-to-start-an-ecommerce-business-without-spending-any-money) , create a Shopify store and integrate a print-on-demand app such as Printful, Gelato, or Printify. With print on demand, you pay nothing upfront for inventory—products are manufactured only after customers place orders. This eliminates inventory risk and lets you test multiple designs with minimal financial commitment. Focus your initial budget on creating quality designs and basic marketing to drive traffic to your store.
